edition.locus: Against Marcion 1.9 (unknown god cannot be; prove uncertain by the known)

source_text: Scio quidem, quo sensu nouum deum iactitent, agnitione utique. sed ipsam nouitatem cognitionis percutientem\', rudes animas ipsamque naturalem nouitatis gratiositatem uolui repercutere, et hinc iam de ignoto deo prouocare. utique enim quem agnitione nouum opponunt, ignotum ante agnitionem demonstrant. age igitur, ad lineas rursum et in gradum! per-I suade deum ignotum esse potuisse. inuenio plane ignotis deis aras prostitutas, sed Attica idolatria est. item incertis deis, sed superstitio Romana est. porro incerti dei minus noti, ut minus certi, et proinde ignoti, qua minus certi. quem titulum incidemus ex duobus deo Marcionis? utrumque, opinor, et nunc incerto et retro ignoto. sicut enim ignotum eum fecit deus notus, creator, ita et incertum deus certus. sed non euagabor, uti dicam: deus si ignotus fuit latuitque, illum regio latebrarum obumbrauit, noua utique et ipsa et ignota et similiter nunc quoque incerta, certe inmensa aliqua et maior indubitate eo, quem abscondit. sed breuiter proponam et plenissime exequar, praescribens deum ignorari nec potuisse nomine magnitudinis nec debuisse nomine benignitatis, praesertim in utroque praelatiorem nostro creatore. sed quoniam animaduerto in quibusdam ad formam creatoris prouocari oportere omnis dei noui et retro ignoti probationem, hoc ipsum ratione fieri a nobis prius commendare debebo, quo constantius utar rationis editae patrocinio. ante omnia quidem quale est, ut qui deum agnoscis creatorem et priorem de notitia confiteris, non eisdem modis et alium scias tibi examinandum, quibus iam in alio didicisti deum nosse? omnis res anterior posteriori normam praeministrauit. duo nunc dei proponuntur, ignotus et notus. de noto uacat quaestio. esse eum constat, quia notus non fuisset nisi esset. de ignoto instat altercatio. potest enim et non esse, quia si esset, notus fuisset. quod ergo quaeritur, quamdiu ignoratur, in incerto est, quamdiu quaeritur, et potest non esse, quamdiu in incerto est. habes deum certum, qua notum, et incertum, qua ignotum. si ita est, ecquid tibi uidetur iusta ratione defendi, ut ad normam et formam et regulam certorum probentur incerta? ceterum si ad hanc causam, et ipsam adhuc incertam, etiam argumenta de incertis adhibeantur, series implicabitur quaestionum ex ipsorum quoque argumentorum aeque incertorum retractatu periclitantium de fide per incertum, et ibitur in illas iam indeterminabiles quaestiones, quas apostolus non amat; sin de certis et indubitatis et absolutis regulae partibus, incertis et dubiis et inexpeditis praeiudicabunt. plane in quibus diuersitas status inuenitur, fortassean non prouocentur incerta ad formam certorum, ut liberata a reliqua comparationis prouocatione per diuersitatem status principalis. cum uero duo dii proponuntur, communis est illis status principalis. quod enim deus est, ambo sunt: innati infecti aeterni. hic erit status principalis; cetera uiderit Marcion, si in diuersitate disposuit. posteriora enim (non) sunt in retractatu, immo nec admittentur, si de principali statu constet. porro constat, quia dii ambo: et ita de quorum statu constat communem esse.i cum sub eo ad probationem deuocantur si incerta sunt. ad eorum certorum formam prouocanda erunt, cum quibus de communione status principalis censentur, ut proinde et de probatione communicent. hinc itaque constantissime diri-: gam deum non esse, qui sit hodie incertus, quia retro ignotus, quando quem constat esse ex hoc ipso constet quod numquam fuerit ignotus, [ideo nec incertus]
pass_a_gloss: Nouus agnitione = ante ignotus. Incerta ad normam certi. Qui ignotus, non deus.
pass_b_english: I know indeed in what sense they toss about a new god—by recognition of course. But I wanted to strike back the very novelty of cognition striking rude souls and the very natural graciousness of novelty, and from here already to challenge about the unknown god. For of course whom they oppose as new by recognition, they show unknown before recognition. Come then, back to the lines and into step! Persuade that a god could have been unknown. I find plainly altars prostituted to unknown gods—but that is Attic idolatry. Likewise to uncertain gods—but that is Roman superstition. Further, uncertain gods are less known, as less certain, and accordingly unknown, inasmuch as less certain. What title shall we cut from the two for Marcion’s god? Both, I suppose—both now uncertain and formerly unknown. For just as the known God, the Creator, made him unknown, so also the certain God made him uncertain.

But I will not wander off so as to say: if a god was unknown and hid, a region of hiding overshadowed him—new of course itself too and unknown and likewise now also uncertain, certainly some immense and indubitably greater than him whom it hid. But I will briefly propose and most fully pursue, prescribing that a god could not have been unknown by the name of greatness nor ought to have been by the name of kindness—especially more outstanding in both than our Creator. But since I notice that in some things the proving of every new and formerly unknown god ought to be challenged to the Creator’s form, I ought first to commend that this itself is done by us with reason, so that I may more constantly use the patronage of the reason set forth.

Before all things indeed what sort of thing is it that you who recognize God the Creator and confess him prior from knowledge do not know that another is also to be examined for you by the same modes by which you already learned to know God in another? Every prior thing has furnished a norm to the later. Two gods are now proposed, unknown and known. About the known the question is vacant. That he is stands firm, because he would not have been known unless he were. About the unknown dispute presses. For he can also not be, because if he were, he would have been known. What therefore is sought, as long as it is unknown, is in uncertainty; as long as it is sought, and can not be, as long as it is in uncertainty. You have a certain god, inasmuch as known, and an uncertain, inasmuch as unknown. If so, does it not seem to you defended by just reason that uncertain things be proved to the norm and form and rule of certain things?

Otherwise if to this cause, itself still uncertain, arguments also from uncertain things are applied, a series of questions will be entangled from the rehandling also of the arguments themselves equally uncertain, risking about faith through uncertainty, and it will go into those already indeterminable questions which the apostle does not love; but if from certain and undoubted and absolute parts of the rule, they will prejudge uncertain and doubtful and unexpedited things. Plainly in things where diversity of status is found, perhaps uncertain things are not challenged to the form of certain, as freed from the remaining challenge of comparison through diversity of principal status. But when two gods are proposed, the principal status is common to them. For what God is, both are: unborn, unmade, eternal. This will be the principal status; let Marcion see to the rest, if he has arranged them in diversity. For later things are not in rehandling—nay will not even be admitted—if it stands about the principal status. Further it stands, because both are gods: and so of those about whose status it stands that it is common. When under it they are called to proof, if they are uncertain, they will have to be challenged to the form of those certain with whom they are counted concerning communion of principal status, so that accordingly they may also share concerning proof. From here therefore most constantly I will direct that he is not God who is today uncertain, because formerly unknown—when he whom it stands to be stands from this itself that he was never unknown, [and therefore not uncertain].
